title: Align xtask interactive scaffolding to .cbd templates

in: Interactive scaffolding for `cbd new-task`, `cbd new-epic`, and `cbd new-review` renders from the corresponding .cbd templates.
Prompted inputs replace the matching template section bodies while preserving headings.
Tests prove template-driven rendering and placeholder replacement.
out: Add new CLI flags or subcommands.

preconditions.statement: The template file .cbd/tasks/TEMPLATE.md exists and is readable.

postconditions.statement: The generated task file is rendered from .cbd/tasks/TEMPLATE.md and preserves all template headings in the same order.
Template placeholders (<ID>, <short title>) are replaced with the provided task id and short title values.

Non-empty prompt responses replace the body content of their corresponding sections (Goal, User story, In scope, Out of scope, Acceptance scenarios (examples-first), Context, Constraints, Dependencies, Unknowns); unprompted sections (Observability (optional)) retain the template defaults unchanged.

preconditions.statement: The template file .cbd/requirements/TEMPLATE.epic.md exists and is readable.

postconditions.statement: The generated epic file is rendered from .cbd/requirements/TEMPLATE.epic.md and preserves all template headings in the same order.
Template placeholders (<EPIC_ID>, <TITLE>, <slug>, <epic_id>) are replaced with the provided epic id, title, and slug values.

Non-empty prompt responses replace the body content of their corresponding sections (Problem, Target users / stakeholders, Goals (outcomes), Success metrics, In scope, Out of scope / Non-goals, Constraints, Integrations / dependencies, User stories, Acceptance scenarios (examples-first), Open questions); unprompted sections (Architectural forks (ADRs), C4 notes (optional), Task backlog) retain the template defaults unchanged.

preconditions.statement: The template file .cbd/reviews/TEMPLATE/review.seed.md exists and is readable.

postconditions.statement: The generated review seed is rendered from .cbd/reviews/TEMPLATE/review.seed.md and preserves all template headings in the same order.
Template placeholders (<REVIEW_ID>, <TITLE>) are replaced with the provided review id and title values.

Non-empty prompt responses replace the body content of their corresponding sections (What is being reviewed?, In scope, Out of scope, Assumptions, Primary assets (initial), External systems / integrations, Security / privacy constraints (explicit), Known risks / incidents / history (if any)); unprompted sections (Threat modeling frameworks, System decomposition (components/containers), Architectural forks / ADRs, Review outputs) retain the template defaults unchanged.

acceptance_tests.description: Running `cbd new-task --interactive` renders from the task template, preserves headings, replaces placeholders, and inserts prompted content.
Running `cbd new-epic --interactive` renders from the epic template, preserves headings, replaces placeholders, and inserts prompted content.
Running `cbd new-review --interactive` renders from the review seed template, preserves headings, replaces placeholders, and inserts prompted content.

assumptions: Template section headings are unique and stable for section replacement.
Unprompted sections retain the template defaults without modification.
Template read failures propagate as CLI errors (non-zero exit) without bespoke error codes.
definition_of_done: each clause id in pre/post/invariants/errors has a proof entry in evidence.json
Rust enforcement is authoritative; TypeScript enforcement is UX-only
